speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you have a history of gait and limb ataxia; to understand the underlying cause, where exactly do you feel your balance and coordination are most impaired, and when did these symptoms first begin?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the symptoms are predominantly on the right side, can you tell me if you have experienced any weakness, numbness, or vision changes on that side recently?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: PML (Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy) secondary to natalizumab therapy for Crohn's disease.

I suspect your immune suppression from natalizumab has triggered a rare but serious brain infection. Given your history of difficult-to-control Crohn's disease and recent onset of ataxia, we need to confirm this immediately. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast. REQUEST IMAGES.
